notes.text: Australian housing credit is predominantly variable-rate, and borrowers who fix usually do so for three years or less. The fixed share of outstanding housing credit roughly doubled from about 20% in late 2019 to almost 40% in early 2022, and around two-thirds of those fixed loans expired during 2022 and 2023, so the post-2022 tightening cycle reached household budgets quickly and in full once the low pandemic fixed rates rolled off.

sources.title: Fixed-rate Housing Loans: Monetary Policy Transmission and Financial Stability Risks

notes.text: APRA requires lenders to assess new borrowers at a rate at least 3 percentage points above the loan rate, a buffer it confirmed in July 2025, which caps borrowing capacity well below what current repayments alone would allow. From 1 February 2026 APRA added a debt-to-income limit: no more than 20% of new owner-occupier lending and 20% of new investor lending may be at six times income or more, with loans for new construction exempt, a constraint aimed mainly at highly leveraged investor demand in an upswing.

sources.title: APRA announces update on macroprudential settings
Activation of debt to income limits as a macroprudential policy tool

notes.text: Since 1 October 2025 the federal Home Guarantee Scheme, rebranded the 5% Deposit Scheme, has had no income caps and no limit on places, with property price caps raised, allowing eligible first home buyers to purchase with a 5% deposit backed by a government guarantee. By lowering the deposit hurdle rather than adding supply, the scheme channels additional demand into the price brackets below the caps.

sources.title: Frequently asked questions: Australian Government 5% Deposit Scheme

notes.text: Construction is running well short of the National Housing Accord target of 1.2 million new homes in the five years to June 2029: about 219,000 homes were completed in the first five quarters to September 2025, 18% of the target, and the National Housing Supply and Affordability Council projected in March 2026 that the target would be met only by June 2030. Persistent under-building relative to population growth keeps upward pressure on both prices and rents.

sources.title: Quarterly Report, March 2026
sources.publisher: National Housing Supply and Affordability Council

notes.text: Net overseas migration, the main driver of household formation, fell from a peak of about 538,000 in 2022-23 to 429,000 in 2023-24 and a preliminary 306,000 in 2024-25, easing but not removing pressure on rental demand. Foreign demand for existing homes is also curtailed: foreign persons, including temporary residents and foreign-owned companies, are barred from buying established dwellings from 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2027, subject to a review on extension.

notes.text: The ABS ceased its Residential Property Price Indexes after the December quarter 2021. Its official quarterly successor, Total Value of Dwellings, reports the value of the entire residential stock and a mean dwelling price for each state and territory, released about 12 weeks after quarter end, so it reflects stock values rather than a quality-adjusted index of transaction prices.
